goal: Prevent a qualified exact source revision from requiring a post-qualification source edit merely to enable training.
procedure: Keep optimizer/gradient/GPU authority false in source permanently. Introduce a separate runtime training-authorizer receipt that revalidates the exact CPU/GPU/token/corpus/teacher/mixture/static-proof evidence and opens only the optimizer authority needed by the trainer while keeping FINAL and private-identity gradient closed.
constraints: no source mutation after exact-head runtime receipts
decision_criteria: runtime receipt binds exact source revision and producer
source plan stays false for optimizer/gradient/GPU authority
authority: Transferable builder governance pattern; does not itself authorize Fable user-model training.
validation: Exact-head workflow 35954241662 passed with 257 tests and 217 static obligations.
failure_or_lesson: A builder can deadlock itself if empirical qualification is hash-bound to source but enabling the next phase requires editing that same source. Runtime authority should advance by receipts, not by mutating the qualified implementation.

goal: Ensure model selection and closure cannot silently switch checkpoint, evaluator, source revision, trainer implementation, or authority receipt.
procedure: Hash-bind checkpoint receipts to the exact trainer and training authorization. Bind DEV receipts to the exact evaluator, validation contract, gate registry, proof contract and training plan. Select the first passing checkpoint on a precommitted cadence from one complete linear checkpoint chain. Carry the selected checkpoint, DEV receipt, selector, training-authorizer, FINAL opening authorizer and frozen FINAL evaluator/package hashes through closure.
decision_criteria: every authority transition has exact receipt lineage
off-chain or duplicate DEV receipts fail closed
closure receipt contains complete authority chain
authority: General builder lesson for any generated model stack with staged fitting/evaluation.
validation: Exact-head workflow 35954241662 passed; no optimizer, gradient or FINAL authority was opened by the static suite.
failure_or_lesson: Passing metrics are not enough if the system cannot prove which code, checkpoint and evaluator produced them. Builder-generated models need end-to-end authority lineage, not only model-file hashes.

goal: Prevent runtime convenience values from becoming hidden model-capability ceilings or selection knobs.
procedure: Separate stage completion from invocation step budget. Permit exact-state same-stage continuation. Keep a precommitted nonzero learning-rate floor beyond the scheduler operating horizon. Freeze DEV checkpoint cadence before gradient. Treat microbatch, accumulation, GPU count, native window and stress sizes as measured operating points rather than semantic capability definitions.
decision_criteria: continuation remains trainable after nominal horizon
checkpoint selection surface is fixed before results
authority: Transferable builder design rule; measured operating points may guide execution but cannot define the user's eventual model capability.
validation: Static tests prove the distinction and exact-head CI remains green.
failure_or_lesson: A builder can accidentally cap a model without writing an explicit 'ceiling': zero learning rate after a nominal horizon, non-resumable step budgets, fixed save cadence chosen after results, or hardware assumptions can all create hidden ceilings.

goal: Prevent structural test presence or copied PASS payloads from masquerading as executed qualification.
procedure: Make the static proof auditor run the registered STATIC_REQUIRED pytest nodes itself on a clean exact source checkout, record JUnit collection/failure/error/skip counts, reject skipped required cases, bind the exact CI workflow and CI_REQUIRED receipt set, and hash-bind runtime receipts to their canonical producer implementations.
constraints: clean exact source before and after proof execution
required tests may not be skipped
decision_criteria: required nodes are actually collected and pass
authority: Builder validation lesson. Presence of validation code is not proof that the generated system was actually validated.
validation: Exact-head workflow 35954241662 passed with 257 tests, 217 static obligations and PASS_N0_FULL_PROOF_MATRIX_STATIC_AUDIT.
failure_or_lesson: A builder that only checks that tests or validators exist can certify an unexecuted system. Execution evidence, exact producer identity and fail-closed skip handling belong in the receipt chain.

goal: Stop provenance hardening from becoming its own objective while still closing the concrete P39PN runtime handoff required for a trustworthy N0 empirical run.
procedure: Re-read the successor objective and retrospective, classify future fixes by whether they prevent a false N0 pass, a hidden capability ceiling, topology/artifact mismatch, DEV/FINAL goalpost movement, or a direct full-envelope contradiction. Treat all other provenance-only additions as out of scope. Add one canonical P39PN materialization path that consumes exact CPU-qualified evidence, materializes every optimizer-facing public lane, freezes FINAL-v2 unopened, and emits the full public-mixture audit without optimizer or gradient authority.
constraints: no source edit merely to create more provenance
operating points are not capability ceilings
decision_criteria: static audit has no known unresolved STATIC_REQUIRED defect
new fix must change correctness of the eventual N0 capability claim rather than receipt aesthetics
authority: Transferable builder-governance lesson. Builder validation must be strong enough to protect claims but must stop once additional machinery no longer changes model correctness or phase authority.
validation: Exact-head workflow 35954996471 passed at f78cb119... with 259 tests, 219 STATIC_REQUIRED obligations, and 243 total proof obligations. Remaining blockers are non-static empirical gates.
failure_or_lesson: A builder can fail in two directions: under-validating a system, or over-engineering validation until it displaces the model-building objective. The stop rule is whether a new control prevents a real false-pass or capability error.
